gate_rows.evidence: CBO/JCT define the 90-percent taxable-earnings alternative and publish annual FY2025-FY2034 deficit effects.
The 2026 Trustees report supplies current OASDI depletion, payable-benefit, actuarial-deficit, and taxable-payroll context.
The option raises scheduled benefits for affected workers, but replacement-rate and lifetime-benefit effects by birth and earnings cohort are not populated.
Statutory employee/employer shares do not establish economic incidence, labor-supply response, compensation shifting, or self-employed burden.
The 15-percent age-65-plus SPM poverty baseline exists, but policy and stress values for retirees, survivors, disabled workers, women, and long-lived low earners are absent.
Employer payroll-system changes, self-employment administration, compliance, avoidance, benefit-record changes, and implementation costs are not quantified.
CBO's aggregate score includes an income-tax offset, but TAXLANE lacks tax-unit allocation and joint distribution with the guarded REV instrument.
The December 2024 option has not been rescored on 2026 assumptions and does not establish the post-2034 payable-benefit or 75-year actuarial-balance result.

candidate_decision.next_candidate_strategy: obtain a 2026-baseline actuarial rescore with cohort benefits, incidence, adequacy, administration, and tax-unit overlap allocated jointly with REV

public_warning: Two evidence gates pass, but six cohort, incidence, adequacy, administration, overlap, and rescore gates remain blocked. The option is a serious solvency candidate, not a spending cut and not an additive extension of REV.
